name: Around the Bay
lede: The suburbs and small cities around Tampa in Hillsborough and Pasco counties: Temple Terrace and Plant City, Hillsborough's other incorporated cities; unincorporated Brandon, Riverview, Apollo Beach and Ruskin; and Pasco County's Wesley Chapel, Zephyrhills, Dade City and New Port Richey. Visitors come for the Florida Strawberry Festival, winter manatee viewing at Apollo Beach, spring and river parks, outlet and mall shopping, and Pasco's small Gulf coast towns.
known_for: Lithia Springs and Alafia River parks
Tampa Premium Outlets and The Shops at Wiregrass
notes: Visit Tampa Bay fast facts: 'Three incorporated cities: Tampa (398,000 population), Temple Terrace, & Plant City'; 'Major unincorporated areas: Brandon, Ruskin, Apollo Beach'. Pasco County's tourism office is Florida's Sports Coast (flsportscoast.com), which lists New Port Richey, Dade City, Zephyrhills and Wesley Chapel as its destinations.

name: Gulf Beaches
lede: A chain of barrier islands along Pinellas County's Gulf coast, from Clearwater Beach south through Sand Key, Indian Rocks Beach, Madeira Beach, Treasure Island and St. Pete Beach to Pass-a-Grille and Fort De Soto. Each beach town has its own character, from Clearwater Beach's resorts and Pier 60 to Pass-a-Grille's low-rise historic district and Fort De Soto's county park beaches. Visit St. Pete/Clearwater reported all of its beaches open, with no advisories, on Sep 27, 2026.
notes: Beach conditions page (read Sep 27, 2026): 'All St. Pete-Clearwater beaches are open, with no advisories.' Hurricane Helene and Milton (2024) damage and recovery are handled record by record in the stays and places slices; none of the area pages read for this slice mention it.

name: Clearwater & North Pinellas
lede: Pinellas County's mainland north of St. Petersburg: the City of Clearwater's waterfront downtown and aquarium, and small towns up the coast and around Old Tampa Bay. Scottish-influenced Dunedin has breweries and the ferry-served island state parks, Safety Harbor has springs and a historic resort, Tarpon Springs has its Greek sponge docks, and Palm Harbor's Innisbrook hosts the Valspar Championship.
known_for: Phillies and Blue Jays spring training
notes: Visit St. Pete/Clearwater's communities index: 'Greek flags fly everywhere in Tarpon Springs'; 'Craft beer aficionados will find plenty to sample in this walkable town' (Dunedin). 'ferry-served island state parks': Caladesi Island is reached by ferry from Honeymoon Island (caladesiferry.org).

name: Day Trips
lede: Places beyond the bay that make easy day trips: the Bradenton Area with Anna Maria Island, and Sarasota, to the south; Weeki Wachee and the spring-fed rivers of Hernando and Citrus counties to the north; and Polk County's theme parks, gardens and lakes to the east, between Tampa and Orlando.
known_for: LEGOLAND Florida and Bok Tower Gardens
notes: Official URL is VISIT FLORIDA ('Official state travel, tourism and vacation website for Florida'), since the sheet spans five counties; each area record carries its own county tourism site (Bradenton Area CVB, Visit Sarasota, Florida's Adventure Coast, Visit Central Florida). Directions (south, north, east) are map geography, not quoted; drive times are deliberately not given (no source read).

name: St. Petersburg
lede: St. Petersburg, the second-largest city in the Tampa Bay area, sits on the Pinellas peninsula between Tampa Bay and the Gulf of Mexico. Its downtown waterfront has the St. Pete Pier, the Dalí and other museums along a string of bayfront parks, and Central Avenue runs west through arts districts full of murals, galleries, bars and breweries. Gulfport, a small arts town on Boca Ciega Bay, is on this sheet too.
notes: Wikipedia: population 258,308 (2020), 'the second-most populous city in the Tampa Bay area', nicknamed 'The Sunshine City'. Visit St. Pete/Clearwater is Pinellas County's tourism office (Pinellas County calls it 'the county's main resource for visitors').

name: Tampa
lede: Tampa, the county seat of Hillsborough County and the largest city in the Tampa Bay area, sits on the northern shore of Tampa Bay along the Hillsborough River. Downtown's Riverwalk links museums and parks to the Channel District's aquarium and cruise terminals, the free TECO Line Streetcar runs to Ybor City's cigar-era streets, and Busch Gardens and ZooTampa are in the north of the city.
known_for: Ybor City and its cigar history
notes: Visit Tampa Bay fast facts: 'TECO Historic Streetcar runs between downtown and Ybor City district'; five cruise lines homeport 10 vessels; Tampa population 398,000 (Wikipedia: 403,364 in the 2020 census). The Ybor City page describes the streetcar ride into Ybor as free. Visit Tampa Bay's Cuban sandwich page says it was 'Born in Ybor City in the early 1900s'.
